fixes.fix_description: Added an opt-in --splice_tail flag so the short-term series continues with the published level past the 2005M1 end of the microdata-share window, allowing the sample to extend to 2010M12.
fixes.rationale: The microdata shares used for the adjustment only cover through 2005M1, so the sample-length logic (available = min(len)) silently truncated the entire run at the share-window end and could not reach the paper's 1948-2010 endpoint. Recovering the full sample required understanding how the share window interacts with the truncation logic and adding a deliberate data-extension step (concatenating prefix + adjusted + published tail). That is a localized but non-trivial data-handling change requiring comprehension of the pipeline, not a routine one-minute edit, but it does not alter the core algorithm or rely on unavailable data (the published level exists for the tail).
fixes.reproducibility_impact: Indicates the provided notebook/code as shipped only reproduced results up to the microdata-share window (2005M1) and did not itself extend the series to the full 1948-2010 sample the paper reports. The share-based adjustment window and the full analysis window are mismatched, and the code that bridged them was missing. This is a genuine incompleteness in the published pipeline for the full-sample results, though the fix is conservative (default off preserves notebook behavior) and the extension method is a plausible, documented reconstruction rather than a fabrication.

summary: Only one fix was required, and it is a single localized data-handling gap rather than a fundamental methodological failure. The core two-state estimation algorithm was intact and the fix defaults to off so step-2 behavior matches the notebook exactly. The issue is that the published code only ran cleanly up to the 2005M1 end of the microdata-share window, while the paper's headline sample runs through 2010M12; bridging that gap required understanding the truncation logic and adding a deliberate tail-splice using the published level. This raises it above trivial maintenance to major, and signals that the shipped pipeline was incomplete for reproducing the full-sample results even though the estimation methodology itself is sound and implementable.
